subtopics.title: The Elements — What Economics Is Made Of

questions.question: Economics studies how limited resources satisfy:
options: UNLIMITED needs and wants — wants renewing themselves as fast as they are satisfied
A fixed list of basic needs only

questions.question: The four factors of production are:
options: Natural resources, labour, capital and entrepreneurship

questions.question: The factor-reward pairings run:
options: Rent for labour, wages for capital
Profit for labour, interest for land
Rent for natural resources, wages for labour, interest for capital, profit for entrepreneurship

questions.question: The three basic processes, in order, are:
options: Production, exchange, consumption — every economy runs all three

subtopics.title: The Branches — How the Subject Divides

questions.question: Microeconomics studies:
options: Individual units — one household, one firm, one market and its price

questions.question: "One shop's bread price" versus "the general price level" illustrates:
options: Micro versus MACRO — the close-up against the economy as a whole

questions.question: "Unemployment is 32 percent" and "government should create jobs" are, respectively:
options: POSITIVE (testable description) and NORMATIVE (judgement of what ought to be)

questions.question: Development economics focuses on:
options: Improving the welfare of poor economies — deeply relevant to South Africa

questions.question: The method's loop runs:
CETERIS PARIBUS means:
options: "All other things being equal" — isolating one relationship by holding the rest still in thought

questions.question: Models like the circular flow diagram are useful because:
options: They are deliberate simplifications — false in detail, true in structure — making reality thinkable

questions.question: The honest limits of the method include:
options: People learn and react to predictions — so laws are tendencies, forecasts carry error, and disagreement is normal science

questions.question: Economics is classified as:
options: A SOCIAL science — studying human behaviour in society — that uses scientific method

questions.question: Within the social sciences, economics stands out as:
options: The most QUANTITATIVE member — measuring relentlessly and building mathematical models

questions.question: Economics differs from physics because:
options: It can rarely experiment on whole economies or hold society still — its regularities are tendencies

questions.question: The evidentiary habit matters to citizens because:
options: Claims about policies can be TESTED against data and mechanisms rather than merely believed

questions.question: The whole subject in one sentence:
options: Everybody wants more than there is — economics studies that gap and the arrangements invented to live with it
Money is the root of all trade

questions.question: The gogo baking vetkoek combines:
options: Flour (resources), hands (labour), stove (capital) and the decision to bake — entrepreneurship carrying the risk

questions.question: "Make, swap, use" translates to:
The test that sorts micro from macro:
options: Could you point at it on your street? One taxi fare — micro; the cost of living — macro

questions.question: "Not one person job-hunting but millions" describes:
options: The drone shot — macroeconomics, the economics of everybody at once

questions.question: "Petrol went up by ninety cents" versus "petrol is too expensive":
options: A MEASUREMENT (positive) versus a JUDGEMENT (normative) — label the sentence before arguing

questions.question: Confusing the two kinds of sentence causes:
options: Arguments where one side quotes measurements and the other expresses wishes — both thinking they disagree about facts

subtopics.title: Testing Like a Scientist, Watching People Like a Neighbour

questions.question: The rainy-morning taxi rank example demonstrates:
options: The scientific loop — notice, guess, test, keep what survives — run on street life

questions.question: Ceteris paribus is needed because:
options: In real life everything changes at once — the phrase isolates one thread to think clearly

questions.question: "Water never decides to boil differently because it heard the forecast" points at:
options: Economics' unique subject: people who react to predictions — so its laws are strong tendencies, not certainties

questions.question: Two economists disagreeing on the news is:
options: The sound of a young science working on the hardest material there is: us
